question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=x^{2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2 x\,⟹\,\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u=x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x \sin{\left(x^{2} \right)}\,\text{d}x &=\int \sin{\left(x^{2} \right)}\cdot x\,\text{d}x \\ &=1\int \sin{\left(u \right)}\cdot \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\,\text{d}u \\ &=\frac{1}{2}\int \sin{\left(u \right)}\,\text{d}u \\ &=- \frac{\cos{\left(u \right)}}{2}+C \\ &=- \frac{\cos{\left(x^{2} \right)}}{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u={x}^{3}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3{x}^{2}\,⟹\,\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u={x}^{2}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x^{2} \sec^{2}{\left(x^{3} \right)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \sec^{2}{\left(x^{3} \right)}\cdot x^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =1\int \sec^{2}{\left(u \right)}\cdot \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\int \sec^{2}{\left(u \right)}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{\tan{\left(u \right)}}{3}+C \\  & =\frac{\tan{\left(x^{3} \right)}}{3}+C\end{aligned}

\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2 x\,⟹\,\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u=x\,\text{d}x.

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{\frac{\sqrt{6} \sqrt{\pi}}{6}}^{\frac{\sqrt{2} \sqrt{\pi}}{2}} x \cos{\left(x^{2} \right)}\,\text{d}x & =\int_{\frac{\sqrt{6} \sqrt{\pi}}{6}}^{\frac{\sqrt{2} \sqrt{\pi}}{2}} \cos{\left(x^{2} \right)}\cdot x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \cos{\left(u \right)}\cdot \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \cos{\left(u \right)}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{\sin{\left(u \right)}}{2}\big|_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\left(\sin{\left(\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) \right)}-\left(\sin{\left(\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) \right)}\right)\right) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
